front: Friday's nine-game slate had two routs, San Antonio by 38 over Golden State and Memphis by 31 over New Orleans, and it was broken open by Alperen Sengun (69.9: 43 on 17-24), Franz Wagner (66.8: 35 and 12 assists), Bam Adebayo (58.3) and Davion Mitchell (55.5 on 17 assists); Yaxel Lendeborg (12.9 in the Spurs rout) and Darius Acuff (32.8 on 6-19) sank their holders. Your 102 teams had a median finish in the top 42%; 7 made the top 10% (below the field's rate) and none the top 1%, and 12 cashed, $112 back on $470. The biggest gap against the field was Sengun: on 7% of your teams against the field's 17%, and on half of the afternoon's top-10% teams against 8% of yours. In the afternoon, where your board and ETR's order split a close call, ETR's side scored more 69% of the time (your board 31%; season 46%, where ETR alone wins), and four of your five T3 moves cost points, three of them putting Black and Siakam ahead of Sabonis and Durant. On the season your T3 moves are 41% right at about 5 points a move against you, so the button's T3 order is the one to follow. Two board changes are live from today: an A5 player whose projection is two tiers higher now lands in T4 VALUE instead of below the cut, and the Swaps button keeps T1-T4 from your PM lock and ranks the top 16 by projection as T5.

moves.3: The afternoon T3 moves all went one way: Black and Siakam (both ETR Bad or shaky reads) raised past Sabonis and Durant, and Lendeborg past Daniels before the rout; Zion over Jerome was the one that paid.

back: Watch the new fresh-absence bump (1.5x the teammate table, from today): last night's two biggest splits on a team with fresh absences (Queen 41.0 against ETR 32.9, Zion 50.8 against 44.9, with Murray and Murphy out) already had our number too high, and ETR was closer.
